proposition.claim:
Appendix A.1 divides each connection group by \(2n_{st}\), while the group key retains both source and target lateralizations. It says the resulting matrix gives identical weights to mirror-related connections while preserving overall strength.

The paper trains an integrator with inputs \(u\in[-U,U]\) and signed decoded angular velocity \(v=\delta\theta(t)\). Its linear-consistency loss takes the variance of \(v/|u|\) around a common mean across nonzero inputs.
proposition.domain: Latest-source comparison of the final proceedings paper, its official supplemental PDF and the current bioRxiv version history, concentrating on the two unresolved definitions. No author implementation or network simulation was executed.
assumptions: The connection key and \(n_{st}\) are interpreted literally as defined in Appendix A.1, with no additional unreported mirror-group merger.
The displayed mean pools both signs of nonzero \(u\), and \(\delta\theta(t)\) retains its signed meaning rather than a magnitude or a direction-normalized value.
